newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Diagonal bear spread bought in BT.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Diagonal bear spread bought in BT.

text.p: Traded options in British Telecommunications were the busiest stock option class by early afternoon on Wednesday, dealers said.

This was due to a number of spread trades in BT put options. The biggest of these concerned the sale of 2,800 May 420 puts at 6p and the purchase of 2,800 August 460 puts at 46p for a net debit of 40p in a diagonal bear spread.

If the underlying shares fall to 420p by May expiry the short puts will be worthless and because the August puts will still have some time value, the spread will widen to more than the 40p debit amount so the position can be closed at a profit.
The August puts might still be kept if it is believed BT shares will fall further between May and August expiry dates.

But if BT shares go substantially higher by May expiry the spread between the options will reduce to less than 40p -- because the put premiums will converge -- and the strategy will make a loss at that stage.
Another large deal in BT was a crossed trade in the same diagonal spread which involved trading about 2,000 lots in the same options series and at the same option prices.
By 1340 GMT, BT shares had slipped 1-1/2p to 435p.
The biggest deal in mining group RTZ was from a seller of 500 May 950 calls at 37-1/2p. RTZ shares fell 2p to 978-1/2p.
Over in FTSE 100 index options the main deals were volatility trades. One such deal was the purchase of about 1,000 June 4300 calls at 210-1/2p against the sale of March FTSE futures at 4419.
By 1340 GMT, spot FTSE was down 10.4 to 4433.9 and March futures were down 12 points to 4419.
